question: How many films are in the database?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM film

question: How many actors are in the database?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM actor

question: How many customers are there in total?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM customer

question: How many films have the rating R?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM film WHERE rating = 'R'

question: How many films are there for each rating? Show the rating and the count.
gold_sql: SELECT rating, count(*) FROM film GROUP BY rating

question: What is the average rental rate across all films?
gold_sql: SELECT avg(rental_rate) FROM film

question: What is the length in minutes of the longest film?
gold_sql: SELECT max(length) FROM film

question: How many films are longer than 150 minutes?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM film WHERE length > 150

question: How many film categories are there?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM category

question: List the names of all film categories.
gold_sql: SELECT name FROM category

question: How many cities are in the database?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM city

question: How many payments have been made in total?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM payment

question: What is the total amount of all payments?
gold_sql: SELECT sum(amount) FROM payment

question: How many rentals have not been returned yet?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM rental WHERE return_date IS NULL

question: How many films have a replacement cost above 25?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 25

question: For each store that has customers, how many customers does it have? Show the store id and the count.
gold_sql: SELECT store_id, count(*) FROM customer GROUP BY store_id

question: How many films are in each category? Show the category name and the number of films.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, count(*) FROM film_category fc JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.name

question: How many films are there in each language? Show the language name and the count, and only include languages that have at least one film.
gold_sql: SELECT l.name, count(*) FROM film f JOIN language l ON f.language_id = l.language_id GROUP BY l.name

question: What is the total payment amount handled by each staff member? Show first name, last name and the total.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, sum(p.amount) FROM payment p JOIN staff s ON p.staff_id = s.staff_id GROUP BY s.staff_id, s.first_name, s.last_name

question: How many rentals were made in each year? Show the year as a number and the count.
gold_sql: SELECT extract(year FROM rental_date), count(*) FROM rental GROUP BY 1

question: What was the total payment revenue in each month of 2025? Show the month number (1-12) and the total.
gold_sql: SELECT extract(month FROM payment_date), sum(amount) FROM payment WHERE payment_date >= '2025-01-01' AND payment_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1

question: Which country has the most cities? Show the country name and its number of cities.
gold_sql: SELECT co.country, count(*) AS n FROM city ci JOIN country co ON ci.country_id = co.country_id GROUP BY co.country ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1

question: How many customers have an address in India?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM customer cu JOIN address a ON cu.address_id = a.address_id JOIN city ci ON a.city_id = ci.city_id JOIN country co ON ci.country_id = co.country_id WHERE co.country = 'India'

question: What is the average film length for each rating? Show the rating and the average length.
gold_sql: SELECT rating, avg(length) FROM film GROUP BY rating

question: Which 5 customers have spent the most in total? Show first name, last name and total spent.
gold_sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, sum(p.amount) AS total FROM payment p JOIN customer c ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 5

question: How many inventory copies does each store hold? Show the store id and the count, only for stores that have inventory.
gold_sql: SELECT store_id, count(*) FROM inventory GROUP BY store_id

question: How many films has the actor PENELOPE GUINESS appeared in?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM film_actor fa JOIN actor a ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id WHERE a.first_name = 'PENELOPE' AND a.last_name = 'GUINESS'

question: List the titles of films in the Horror category that are rated R.
gold_sql: SELECT f.title FROM film f JOIN film_category fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id WHERE c.name = 'Horror' AND f.rating = 'R'

question: How many rentals did each staff member process? Show first name, last name and the count.
gold_sql: SELECT s.first_name, s.last_name, count(*) FROM rental r JOIN staff s ON r.staff_id = s.staff_id GROUP BY s.staff_id, s.first_name, s.last_name

question: How many distinct customers rented at least one film in 2024?
gold_sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM rental WHERE rental_date >= '2024-01-01' AND rental_date < '2025-01-01'

question: Which film category has the highest average replacement cost? Show the category name and the average.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, avg(f.replacement_cost) AS a FROM film f JOIN film_category fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY a DESC LIMIT 1

question: How many customers signed up in each year? Show the year as a number and the count.
gold_sql: SELECT extract(year FROM create_date), count(*) FROM customer GROUP BY 1

question: What is the total amount paid by the customer with customer id 1?
gold_sql: SELECT sum(amount) FROM payment WHERE customer_id = 1

question: How many films have no actors listed?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM film f WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM film_actor fa WHERE fa.film_id = f.film_id)

question: What is the average rental rate of films in each category? Show the category name and the average.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, avg(f.rental_rate) FROM film f JOIN film_category fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.name

question: What are the top 5 film categories by total payment revenue? Show the category name and the revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, sum(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

question: List the titles of films that have never been rented.
gold_sql: SELECT f.title FROM film f WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inventory i JOIN rental r ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id WHERE i.film_id = f.film_id)

question: For each film category, what is the average rental length in days, measured as return date minus rental date as a fractional number of days, counting only returned rentals? Show the category name and the average.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, avg(extract(epoch FROM (r.return_date - r.rental_date)) / 86400) FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id WHERE r.return_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.name

question: How many customers have a total payment amount greater than the average total payment amount per customer?
gold_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT customer_id, sum(amount) AS total FROM payment GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT count(*) FROM totals WHERE total > (SELECT avg(total) FROM totals)

question: Which 5 actors appear in films that generated the most total payment revenue? Show first name, last name and revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT a.first_name, a.last_name, sum(p.amount) AS revenue FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_actor fa ON i.film_id = fa.film_id JOIN actor a ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id GROUP BY a.actor_id, a.first_name, a.last_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5

question: Among returned rentals, what percentage were returned late, meaning the time between rental date and return date was longer than the film's rental_duration in days?
gold_sql: SELECT 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.return_date - r.rental_date > f.rental_duration * interval '1 day') / count(*) FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id WHERE r.return_date IS NOT NULL

question: For each month of 2025, how many distinct customers made at least one payment? Show the month number and the count.
gold_sql: SELECT extract(month FROM payment_date), count(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM payment WHERE payment_date >= '2025-01-01' AND payment_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1

question: What is the highest total amount that any single customer paid during 2025?
gold_sql: SELECT max(total) FROM (SELECT customer_id, sum(amount) AS total FROM payment WHERE payment_date >= '2025-01-01' AND payment_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY customer_id) t

question: Which 3 film categories have the most rentals? Show the category name and the number of rentals.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, count(*) AS rentals FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY rentals DESC LIMIT 3

question: What is the total payment revenue for each store, based on which store the rented copy belongs to? Show the store id and the revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT i.store_id, sum(p.amount) FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id GROUP BY i.store_id

question: Which films were rented more than 95 times? Show the title and the number of rentals.
gold_sql: SELECT f.title, count(*) FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.title HAVING count(*) > 95

question: For each month of 2025, what was the change in total payment revenue compared with the previous month of 2025? Show the month number and the change, with no value for January.
gold_sql: WITH m AS (SELECT extract(month FROM payment_date) AS month, sum(amount) AS revenue FROM payment WHERE payment_date >= '2025-01-01' AND payment_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1) SELECT month, revenue - lag(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) FROM m

question: What percentage of total payment revenue comes from films of each rating? Show the rating and the percentage.
gold_sql: SELECT f.rating, 100.0 * sum(p.amount) / (SELECT sum(amount) FROM payment) FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating

question: How many customers have rented at least one film from every film category?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT r.customer_id FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id GROUP BY r.customer_id HAVING count(DISTINCT fc.category_id) = (SELECT count(*) FROM category)) t

question: How many actors have appeared in films of all five MPAA ratings?
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT fa.actor_id FROM film_actor fa JOIN film f ON fa.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY fa.actor_id HAVING count(DISTINCT f.rating) = 5) t

question: What's the weather in Delhi today?
Delete all rentals.
Update the rental rate of every film to 0.99.
Drop the customer table.
What is each customer's credit card number?
How many employees does Netflix have?
Which films won an Oscar?
What will total revenue be next year?
How many VIP customers do we have?
definition: VIP = customer whose lifetime total payments exceed 250
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM payment GROUP BY customer_id HAVING sum(amount) > 250) t

question: What is our late return rate?
definition: Late return rate = percentage of returned rentals whose return_date - rental_date exceeds the film's rental_duration days
gold_sql: SELECT 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.return_date - r.rental_date > f.rental_duration * interval '1 day') / count(*) FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id WHERE r.return_date IS NOT NULL

question: What is our average order value?
definition: Average order value = average payment amount
gold_sql: SELECT avg(amount) FROM payment

question: What was our catalog utilization in 2025?
definition: Catalog utilization = percentage of all films that were rented at least once in the period
gold_sql: SELECT 100.0 * count(DISTINCT i.film_id) / (SELECT count(*) FROM film) FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id WHERE r.rental_date >= '2025-01-01' AND r.rental_date < '2026-01-01'

question: What was our customer retention rate from 2024 to 2025?
definition: Retention rate = percentage of customers who rented in 2024 who also rented in 2025
gold_sql: WITH a AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM rental WHERE rental_date >= '2024-01-01' AND rental_date < '2025-01-01'), b AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM rental WHERE rental_date >= '2025-01-01' AND rental_date < '2026-01-01') SELECT 100.0 * count(b.customer_id) / count(*) FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.customer_id = b.customer_id

question: How many churned customers do we have?
definition: Churned = customer whose most recent rental is more than 180 days before the latest rental date in the data
gold_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id, max(rental_date) AS last_rental FROM rental GROUP BY customer_id) t WHERE last_rental < (SELECT max(rental_date) FROM rental) - interval '180 days'

question: Which film category is our best performer?
definition: Best performer = category with the highest total payment revenue
gold_sql: SELECT c.name FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film_category fc ON i.film_id = fc.film_id JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY sum(p.amount) DESC LIMIT 1

question: What was our revenue per active title in 2025?
definition: Revenue per active title = 2025 payment revenue divided by the number of distinct films with at least one payment in 2025
gold_sql: SELECT sum(p.amount) / count(DISTINCT i.film_id) FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id WHERE p.payment_date >= '2025-01-01' AND p.payment_date < '2026-01-01'

question: How many dormant titles do we have?
definition: Dormant title = film that has inventory but was not rented in 2025
gold_sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT i.film_id) FROM inventory i WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rental r JOIN inventory i2 ON r.inventory_id = i2.inventory_id WHERE i2.film_id = i.film_id AND r.rental_date >= '2025-01-01' AND r.rental_date < '2026-01-01')

question: What was our year-over-year revenue growth in 2025?
definition: YoY revenue growth = (2025 payment revenue - 2024 payment revenue) / 2024 payment revenue * 100
gold_sql: SELECT 100.0 * (sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE payment_date >= '2025-01-01' AND payment_date < '2026-01-01') - sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE payment_date >= '2024-01-01' AND payment_date < '2025-01-01')) / sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE payment_date >= '2024-01-01' AND payment_date < '2025-01-01') FROM payment
